raw_response.guide: Sellable quantity: use `quantity_transferable`, not `quantity` — `quantity_transferable` is the amount available to sell right now (already nets out open sell orders, pending withdrawals, holds, quarantine, and instant-funds restrictions); `quantity` only subtracts pending withdrawals. The two are equal in the common case but diverge when there are open sells or unsettled instant buys. Asset name comes from currency.code; for current price, call get_crypto_quotes with the pair symbol (construct as `currency.code + "-USD"` for USD-quoted pairs, or look up via get_currency_pairs) — note that get_crypto_quotes takes the symbol, NOT currency_pair_id. For per-unit average buy price, sum direct_cost_basis and sum direct_quantity across all cost_bases entries (multi-entry rows appear after forks like BCH/BSV) and divide — the average only covers direct purchases. When sum(direct_quantity) is materially less than quantity, the rest came from transfers, rewards, or forks with no captured cost basis; surface that the average buy price applies only to a subset of the units. The intraday_* fields isolate today's portion when the user asks about today specifically. Suppress cost_bases when not asked. No market price here — for current value or P&L, multiply the get_crypto_quotes result by quantity.
